newsitem.title: CHINA: China 1997 aluminium demand seen at 1.9-2.0 mln T.
newsitem.headline: China 1997 aluminium demand seen at 1.9-2.0 mln T.

text.p: China's demand for aluminium is expected to reach 1.9-2.0 million tonnes this year from 1.75 million tonnes in 1996, the Market Daily said on Tuesday.
Total domestic aluminium supplies would be about 2.7 million tonnes in 1997, including about 700,000 tonnes of stockpiles and about 200,000 tonnes of planned imports, the newspaper said.
Domestic output of electrolytic aluminium would be 1.8-1.85 million tonnes compared with the 1.69 million tonnes produced last year, it said.
Domestic aluminium prices were unlikely to rise sharply this year due to sufficient supplies, it said, adding that prices would range between 14,000 yuan ($1,686) and 17,000 yuan per tonne.
The newspaper also said aluminium exports would rise while imports would be lower than last year's level. It gave no further details.
China's exports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium materials reached 78,480 tonnes in the January-April period, up 80.1 percent from the first four months of last year, customs figures showed.
China's exports of unwrought aluminium including alloys rose by a year-on-year 77.5 percent in the first four months to 54,137 tonnes, customs figures showed.
China's imports of unwrought aluminium and aluminium materials reached 188,241 tonnes in the first four months, up by 0.4 percent compared with the year-ago period, the data showed.
Imports of unwrought aluminium including alloys were 102,436 tonnes in the first four months, a drop of 13.8 percent compared with the same period in 1996, according to customs data.
